children: , the global payments and financial-technology network, unveiled a Know-Your-Agent initiative with Visa and Ant International on Thursday. Shares slipped approximately 0.4% to $565.095 in morning trading. The chart shows the stock trading 17% below its GF Value estimate of $680.81, pointing to a potentially meaningful valuation gap.

The project tackles a basic problem in agentic commerce: how can merchants trust software that shops on a customer's behalf? Through the Monetary Authority of Singapore-backed BuildFin.ai platform, the companies plan to connect Mastercard Verifiable Intent, Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol and Ant International's Agentic Mobile Protocol. Card networks, digital wallets, marketplaces and AI platforms could then identify approved purchasing agents without surrendering control of their own authorization rules.

Mastercard handled 47.4 billion switched transactions last quarter and generated $9.28 billion in revenue. AI agents could eventually bring more purchasing activity onto its network, but they also create a thorny question: who pays when autonomous software authorizes the wrong transaction? Shared identity standards may reduce fraud and confusion, yet investors still lack an adoption timetable, a defined revenue model and clear rules for allocating losses.

title: Mastercard's AI Checkout Pact Targets the Internet's Next Fraud Problem
